title: Training: a lost node and a hung rank, with nobody there
purpose: Take one GPU node away from a running job, then freeze one rank mid-run. The job must restart itself and resume from checkpoints each time, with bounded lost work.

steps.display: kubectl create -f trainjob.yaml   # s05: 2 nodes x 1 GPU, 600 steps, checkpoint every 50 (async)

steps.output: job is at step about 150; the node holding rank 1 is i-010fd73f6354562aa (NodeClaim gpu-training-pqhgd)

steps.display: kubectl delete nodeclaim gpu-training-pqhgd   # the node under rank 1 is taken away while the job runs
kubectl -n llm-train get jobset s05   # restarts counter
steps.output:
NAME   TERMINALSTATE   RESTARTS   COMPLETED   SUSPENDED   STARTTIME   AGE
s05                    1                      false                   9m22s

steps.display: what the job did on its own
steps.output: resumed from checkpoint at step 150 after 240 s (a replacement GPU node was bought and the image pulled)

steps.display: kubectl -n llm-train exec s05-node-0-1-gnqk9 -- python -c '<SIGSTOP the training process>'   # rank 1 freezes; it does not crash

steps.output:
NAME                                STATE      AGE
trainjob.trainer.kubeflow.org/s05   Complete   17m

NAME                         TERMINALSTATE   RESTARTS   COMPLETED   SUSPENDED   STARTTIME   AGE
jobset.jobset.x-k8s.io/s05   Completed       2          True        false                   17m

steps.display: every attempt, from the events in S3

steps.output:
wall time from first start to done: 837 s
median step time 0.82 s (0.39 s of compute plus the 0.45 s delay I added per step so the run lasts long enough to interfere with)
productive time (600 steps): 490 s
goodput: 59% of the wall time
steps recomputed: about 0 after the node loss (the live step count can lag by a scrape), 33 after the hang

checks.description: after the node loss the job restarted itself and resumed from a checkpoint, not from step 0
checks.because: JobSet's failure policy restarts the whole group; the script finds the newest complete checkpoint in S3 and loads it.

checks.description: the work lost to the failure is at most one checkpoint interval (50 steps)
checks.because: Prometheus said step 150 just before the node was removed (it can be one 10-second scrape, about 12 steps, behind) and the job resumed from step 150.
SIGSTOP freezes the process without ending it, which is what a stuck collective looks like to Kubernetes: nothing fails.

checks.description: the watchdog noticed that no step had completed for 60 seconds and ended the process
checks.because: A frozen peer leaves rank 0 waiting in a collective forever. Its own timer is the only thing that can notice.

checks.description: the job finished all 600 steps after two disruptions without anyone touching it
checks.because: JobSet restarted the group 2 times; each restart resumed from the newest checkpoint.

checks.description: the second restart also resumed from a checkpoint
checks.because: The hang restart read the checkpoints the first attempt had written.

checks.description: the work lost to the hang is also at most one checkpoint interval
checks.because: The watchdog fired at step 233 and the job resumed from step 200.
Goodput is the share of wall time that produced new steps, after restarts, replacement nodes, image pulls and lost work.
